evidence: The current issue asks for a shortcut to turn off the display without sleeping while rendering continues.
#39287 is open, assigned, and requests turning off the display while keeping the system awake, with input waking the display.
Awake currently uses SetThreadExecutionState to request system/display awake states; it does not implement an instant display-off command.
judgment.recommended_action: Post a duplicate response directing the reporter to #39287 and close this parallel request.

issue_context.summary: The reporter wants an immediate keyboard command to power down the display during long rendering while leaving the computer and workload running.
known_information: The display should wake on mouse, touch, or keyboard input.
The scenario is overnight video rendering with disruptive monitor light.
Issue #39287 already tracks turning off the screen while keeping the system awake.
inferences: Awake may not ultimately be the owning module because its current responsibility is preventing sleep rather than commanding display power-off.
issue_context.analysis: This is an exact product-level duplicate of #39287, not a new bug needing separate diagnostics. Consolidating the request avoids splitting the architectural discussion about Awake versus another utility.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the complete issue and triage comment; there are no assignees or linked fixes.
Compared open issues #39287, #49821, and #47488; #39287 most closely matches the requested behavior and wake-on-input scenario.
Inspected Awake/Core/Manager.cs and Awake/Core/Native/Bridge.cs: current behavior controls execution-state requirements rather than issuing an immediate monitor power-off command.

comment.body: Thanks for the clear rendering/sleep scenario. The same request—turn the display off immediately while keeping the system awake and let normal input wake the screen—is already tracked in #39287. Related display-power work is also discussed in #49821 and #47488. To keep the product ownership and implementation discussion in one place, this issue should be closed as a duplicate of #39287.
